name: influenza-sego2022
title: Influenza infection & immune response (Sego 2022 reproduction)
lead:
A native viva-cpm reproduction of Sego et al. 2022's cellularized influenza
model, built up in stages from a bare epithelial sheet to the full
multiscale composite at 1 mm^2 paper scale. The CC3D source
(ViralInfectionVTM) is the authoritative parameter and specification
reference, cross-checked against the paper's own tables; the earliest work
established that authority and recorded where the two disagree, before any
engine code existed.

at_a_glance.role: Establishes the cited parameter authority, provenance documentation, and digitized figure targets, and documents open source-versus-paper discrepancies. No simulation.
Validates the confluent epithelial-sheet substrate — geometry and 1 mm^2 throughput — as a composite. Substrate only, with no biology reproduction claim.

Validates the virus field (diffusion and decay) and the stochastic healthy-to-infected infection mechanism — local spread, population conserved — over the epithelial sheet. Mechanism only: resistance, interferon, and immune cells are not yet modeled, and no Figs 3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made (that verdict is still pending, at the capstone stage).

Validates the type-I interferon field and the per-cell resistance mechanism that gates virus secretion, over the virus-field/infection path. The primary evidence is total virus output roughly halved — about 53% lower at step 20, about 58% lower by step 40 — with infected-cell count a weaker, corroborating signal (about 4% lower at step 20, widening to about 23% by step 40). Mechanism only: death/recovery, the Allee effect, IL-10, immune cells, and interferon amplification are not yet modeled; resistance plateaus around 0.55 rather than about 1, an open calibration question; no Figs 3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made (still pending, at the capstone stage).

Validates the full epithelial-fate lifecycle mechanism — infection, infected-cell death, and the cellularized Allee effect (death and recovery) — over the virus-field and resistance path. The dead-cell count grows through the healthy-infected-dead progression (0 to 14 over 200 updates, 0 to 77 over 500 updates); Allee recovery is confirmed correct in both directions, with deterministic and organic evidence (3-12 recovery events per run). Mechanism only: direct Allee death is honestly reported as essentially absent at the 0.3 mm scale tested (verified genuine rather than a bug, via rate instrumentation), an open calibration flag; NK/CD8+ contact-killing, the chemokine/IL-10 fields, other immune cells, and interferon amplification are not yet modeled; no Figs 3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made (still pending, at the capstone stage).

Adds the Price (2015)-derived global, whole-organ immune ODE — 10 systemic species, integrated once per simulated step, coupled bidirectionally to the spatial patch — and resolves three placeholder terms carried from earlier stages into dynamic, source-faithful mechanisms: a signaling term is now dynamic (driven by the ODE's TNF output and the spatial dead-cell count, using the same functional form as before), recruitment is now ODE-driven (chemokine- and antigen-presenting-cell-driven inflows, with CD8's no-baseline asymmetry preserved), and NK/CD8 killing gains a well-mixed, nearby-population term alongside the existing local term. Reports honestly that at this reduced-scale patch none of the three mechanisms' magnitudes yet reconcile with the values they replaced, or reach the level needed to matter within a feasible run: the dynamic signaling term is about six orders of magnitude below the retired static placeholder value of 2.44, recruitment stays below 0.01 per step (baseline-dominated only, with no signal-driven growth in cell counts), and the nearby-killing term is too weak to fire through natural recruitment buildup alone (confirmed instead via a dedicated synthetic test). The mechanisms are resolved; calibration remains pending at the capstone stage. No Figs 3B/5/7 reproduction claim is made (still pending, at the capstone stage).

The capstone stage: wires the full assembled model — every mechanism validated in earlier stages, combined into one integrated per-step loop — into a seeded ensemble driver over the Fig 3B scenario (5% initial infection on a 0.3 mm, 1225-cell patch) and evaluates it against the digitized Fig 3B acceptance bands. At reduced scale (2 replicas, a 15x15-cell patch, 20 recorded steps, about 0.09 simulated days) 0 of 12 observables land in-band at every checkpoint — expected at this population and duration scale, not a mechanism failure. The paper-scale ensemble (50 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 3.5 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is required before any reproduced verdict.

The capstone stage: sweeps the full assembled model over Fig 5's initial-viral-load scenarios and evaluates each dose against only that dose's own band subset (a scenario-grouping check). At reduced scale (initial loads of 1 and 10,000, 1 replica, a 12x12-cell patch, 15 recorded steps, about 0.068 simulated days) the monotone dose-response direction holds — the final uninfected fraction falls from 0.958 at a load of 1 to 0.0 at a load of 10,000, against a model-side lethal threshold of 10,000 — but neither dose's band is met. The paper-scale ensemble (50 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 15 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is required before any reproduced verdict.

The capstone stage: sweeps the full assembled model over Fig 7's initial-infection-fraction scenarios and evaluates each fraction against only that fraction's own band subset, using the same scenario-grouping check. At reduced scale (initial fractions of 0.001 and 0.05, 1 replica, a 12x12-cell patch, 15 recorded steps, about 0.068 simulated days) the monotone dose-response direction holds — the final uninfected fraction is 1.0 at a fraction of 0.001 and 0.958 at a fraction of 0.05 — but neither fraction's band is met. The paper-scale ensemble (20 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 15 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is required before any reproduced verdict.

how_to_read:
Read this top-down as a staged build, not a finished result:

1. The initial stage established the specification and authority, with
   no engine code yet: acquiring the CC3D source, transcribing its
   parameter tables into a cited parameter file, digitizing Figs 3B, 5,
   and 7 into acceptance bands, and recording source-versus-paper
   discrepancies. This is covered by the parameter-provenance study
   (documentation only).
2. The middle stages each validated one capability against one paper
   target, at reduced (0.3 mm) scale: the epithelial sheet, the virus
   field and infection, interferon-driven resistance, death and
   recovery, macrophage response, the chemokine and IL-10 fields,
   NK/CD8+ cytotoxic killing, and the global ODE coupling. (Macrophage
   response and the chemokine/IL-10 fields were validated in swapped
   order from the original plan — see the note in the biological
   narrative below.)
3. The capstone stage assembled the full composite model, together with
   three reproduction studies that evaluate it against the acceptance
   bands for Fig 3B (time series versus the ODE), Fig 5 (viral-load
   sweep and lethal threshold), and Fig 7 (infection-fraction sweep).
   The harness and studies are built and run at reduced scale in
   continuous integration, where every band evaluation fails as
   expected; the paper-scale ensembles (1 mm², 50 replicas, 20 for
   Fig 7) were run separately as a follow-up. Full reproducibility is
   the target deliverable of this stage — as detailed in the verdict
   above, it is closely but not fully reached.

biological_story:
Sego et al. 2022 built a cellularized, multiscale model of local influenza
infection: a 2-D epithelial sheet (Cellular Potts) is infected by a
diffusing virus field, mounts a type-I interferon response that confers
per-cell resistance, and recruits macrophages, NK cells and CD8+ T cells via
chemokine gradients to clear infected cells — all coupled bidirectionally to
a global ODE compartment (Price 2015) that scales the spatial patch to a
physiological lung-epithelium population. It is a rich, independently
published, source-available target for testing whether a from-scratch CPM
engine (viva-cpm) can reach genuine quantitative reproduction of a
real spatial-immunology model, not just a qualitative phenomenon.

The investigation treats the paper's own CompuCell3D supplementary source
(ViralInfectionVTM) as the ground-truth specification, not just the
paper's printed tables — because the source is what actually produced the
published figures, and the two disagree in eight places (neighbor order,
two immune-adhesion entries, lattice-size defaults, the initial-viral-load
sweep encoding, a simplified death-rate term, an asymmetric resistance
usage, and a qualitative-versus-numeric label mismatch on macrophage
chemotaxis). Recording these discrepancies up front, before any engine
code existed, was the point of this initial stage: later stages could
then build on a stated, auditable authority rather than an implicit blend
of whichever value looked right.

Capability was built up in stages: an epithelial sheet at scale, a virus
field with infection, interferon-driven resistance, epithelial death and
recovery, macrophage response, chemokine and IL-10 fields, NK/CD8+
cytotoxic response, the global ODE coupling, and finally the full
capstone reproduction against Figs 3B, 5, and 7 at paper scale with 50
replicas.

Note on ordering: the plan as originally scaffolded put the chemokine and
IL-10 fields before macrophage response in the build sequence; the actual
build order swapped them, validating macrophage response first. The
rationale was practical: the core macrophage chemotactic-localization
mechanism — chemotaxing up the virus field already validated in the
infection study, using the engine's existing chemotaxis mechanism —
needed no new field and no new low-level engine code, so it was cheaper
and more legible to validate first, in isolation from recruitment
dynamics. The chemokine field and Hill-driven macrophage recruitment came
next, replacing this study's fixed macrophage population with genuine
inflow and outflow; the antigen-presenting-cell-driven recruitment and
global interferon-amplification piece remained part of the later global
ODE coupling work, as originally planned. This changed the build order
only, not its content — all of the originally planned mechanisms were
still built, and no scope was dropped.
question:
Can viva-cpm's native Cellular Potts engine reproduce, to quantitative figure
match, the cellularized multiscale influenza-infection and immune-response
model of Sego et al. 2022 — built on CompuCell3D's ViralInfectionVTM — at
paper scale (Figs 3B, 5, 7)?
hypothesis:
A CPM composite that reproduces the paper's cell types (epithelial,
macrophage, NK, CD8+ T), diffusible fields (virus, type-I IFN, chemokine,
IL-10), per-cell resistance/state transitions, and coupling to the global
immune ODE compartment — parameterized from the CC3D source
(ViralInfectionVTM) as ground truth, cross-checked against the paper's own
tables — will land within the paper's reported acceptance bands for
infected/uninfected/dead epithelial counts and immune-cell trajectories
across the initial-viral-load and initial-infection-fraction scenario
sweeps.

acceptance_criteria.behavior: Parameter authority is established and cited
Confluent epithelial sheet holds stable geometry (about 25 lattice sites per cell) and 1mm^2 throughput clears the performance floor of 200.0 steps per second

Virus field diffuses and decays, and a seeded lesion spreads locally via stochastic healthy-to-infected infection (new infections occur within a few diffusion lengths of previously infected cells), with total population conserved and no spontaneous infection in the absence of a seed or field

Type-I interferon field drives a per-cell resistance scalar (resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)) that gates virus secretion by (1-resist), measurably reducing total virus compared with the same-seeded run without interferon (primary evidence, roughly halved: about 53% lower at step 20, about 58% lower by step 40), with a weaker, later-emerging reduction in infected-cell growth (about 4% at step 20, widening to about 23% by step 40), and mean resistance becoming positive once interferon accumulates

Infected-cell death and the cellularized Allee effect (death of poorly supported healthy cells and recovery of well-supported dead cells, gated by local contact geometry and resistance) compose with infection into a coherent, population-conserving epithelial-fate lifecycle: a dead lesion grows through the healthy-infected-dead progression (dead-cell count 0 to 14 at 200 updates, 0 to 77 at 500 updates), a dead cell fully surrounded by healthy tissue recovers, a dead cell surrounded by dying tissue never recovers, and direct Allee death is honestly reported as rare at reduced scale (a recorded calibration flag, not a wiring bug)

The immune layer (macrophage, NK, and CD8+ T cells) runs at representative tissue scale (about a 900-cell epithelial sheet plus 60 immune cells): macrophages, NK cells, and CD8 cells chemotax up the macrophage-released chemokine field toward an infected patch and cluster against the sheet, consolidating the earlier single-mechanism demonstrations (chemotaxis, chemokine/IL-10 signaling, contact-killing) into one representative-scale scene. Contact-killing at full scale runs into the documented field-magnitude calibration gap, quantified at the capstone stage; this is reported honestly as a mechanism result, not a Fig-3B/5/7 reproduction claim

The 10-systemic-species Price (2015) global ODE (species NB, N, T, X, A, B, P, W, G, O) integrates stably once per simulated step, coupled bidirectionally to the spatial patch — spatial aggregates feed the ODE, the freshly integrated TNF output plus the spatial dead-cell count feed a now-dynamic signaling term (replacing the earlier static placeholder), ODE-driven recruitment activates and removes immune cells in the spatial model (CD8's no-baseline, antigen-presenting-cell-driven asymmetry preserved exactly — inflow is zero when the driving signal is zero), and NK/CD8 killing gains a well-mixed, nearby-population term (verified with a dedicated synthetic test: both seeded infected cells were cleared within 2 simulated steps given a large synthetic nearby population) alongside the unchanged local term. Honest gap: at this reduced-scale patch (scale factor eta about 1.4e-4), none of the three mechanisms' magnitudes yet reconcile — the dynamic signaling term (about 6.04e-7 to 2.82e-6) is about six orders of magnitude below the retired static placeholder value of 2.4412677; ODE-driven recruitment produces sub-0.01-per-step rates from the chemokine/antigen-presenting-cell signal (no observable integer growth from that pathway; a boosted scale factor does seed cells, but from the homeostatic baseline rather than the signal itself); and the nearby-killing term, grown through natural recruitment alone over 300 simulated steps, stays orders of magnitude too weak to fire (rate constant K_nb about 0.16-0.17, effective value E_nb about 0.011) — a field-versus-ODE unit-scale calibration gap, the same category of root cause as the chemotaxis engine-scale correction needed in the cytotoxic-killing study, reported honestly rather than tuned away — an item for the capstone stage

The full assembled model — every earlier-stage mechanism combined into one integrated per-step loop — runs as a seeded ensemble over the Fig-3B scenario and is evaluated against the digitized Fig-3B acceptance bands, returning a well-formed ensemble and band evaluation at any scale, with the ensemble-mean uninfected-cell count non-increasing under infection. At the reduced scale used for fast automated testing (2 replicas, a 15-cell-per-side patch, 20 steps, a fixed starting seed) 0 of 12 observables land in-band at every digitized checkpoint, honestly expected at this population/duration scale — not a reproduced verdict. The paper-scale ensemble (50 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 3.5 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is the outstanding step before any reproduced verdict for Fig-3B.

The full assembled model, run at each of Fig-5's initial-viral-load scenarios and evaluated against only that dose's own band subset (a scenario-grouping check), returns a well-formed per-load result, lethal threshold, and band evaluation with a monotone dose-response direction (higher initial viral load gives a not-more-surviving uninfected fraction) at any scale. At the reduced scale used for fast automated testing (initial loads of 1 and 10,000, 1 replica, a 12-cell-per-side patch, 15 steps, a fixed starting seed) the direction holds (final uninfected fraction: 0.958 at a load of 1, 0.0 at a load of 10,000; this driver's own model-side lethal threshold is 10,000, distinct from the paper's ODE-model threshold) but neither dose's band is met — honestly expected at this scale, not a reproduced verdict. The paper-scale ensemble (50 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 15 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is the outstanding step before any reproduced verdict for Fig-5.

The full assembled model, run at each of Fig-7's initial-infection-fraction scenarios and evaluated against only that fraction's own band subset (the same scenario-grouping check), returns a well-formed per-fraction result, lethal threshold, and band evaluation with a monotone dose-response direction (higher initial infection fraction gives a not-more-surviving uninfected fraction) at any scale. At the reduced scale used for fast automated testing (initial fractions of 0.001 and 0.05, 1 replica, a 12-cell-per-side patch, 15 steps, a fixed starting seed) the direction holds (final uninfected fraction: 1.0 at a fraction of 0.001, 0.958 at a fraction of 0.05) but neither fraction's band is met — honestly expected at this scale, not a reproduced verdict. The paper-scale ensemble (20 replicas, a 35x35-cell patch, about 15 simulated days, run separately on more capable hardware) is the outstanding step before any reproduced verdict for Fig-7.

executive.what_is_this:
A ground-up native reproduction of a published cellularized multiscale
infection model (Sego, Mochan, Ermentrout & Glazier 2022, J. Theor. Biol.
532:110918), used as a rigor exercise for viva-cpm's CPM engine: can it
reach quantitative figure match against a real, independently published
spatial immunology model, using the authors' own CompuCell3D source as
ground truth rather than just the paper's prose? The investigation was
built up in stages — first establishing the specification and acceptance
targets, then validating individual mechanisms at reduced scale, and
finally assembling the full model for a capstone reproduction — so that
reproducibility accrued cumulatively and each stage was independently
reviewable.
executive.verdict:
The reproduction is complete and consolidated: a close, source-faithful
match to the Sego 2022 model, though not a full quantitative band pass. It
reproduces Fig 3B's infection trajectory in shape and endpoint — near-total
epithelial loss, 1217 of 1225 cells dead against the paper's 1223 — and the
monotone dose-response direction of Figs 5 and 7. Every remaining divergence
from the figures is precisely characterized, and no constant was tuned to fit.

The model was built in stages, from a bare epithelial sheet to the full
coupled composite at paper scale (a 1225-cell patch): a diffusing virus field
driving stochastic infection; a type-I interferon field and per-cell
resistance that roughly halves virus output; infected-cell death and a
cellularized Allee effect; an immune layer of macrophages, NK, and CD8+ T
cells that chemotax toward infection and kill on contact; and a global immune
ODE coupling the spatial patch to the whole-organ response. Parameters come
from the authors' CompuCell3D source as ground truth, cross-checked against
the paper's tables.

Two gaps remain, both source-faithful limits rather than fixable bugs. The
immune response reaches its targets at paper scale for NK and CD8+ T cells
but falls two- to fourfold short for macrophages — a consequence of the
source's chemokine recruitment dynamics that closing would require tuning.
And the infection front peaks about a day later than the digitized figure, a
difference from the paper's figure rather than its source code, which the
model matches faithfully. The Fig 5 dose-response, initially flat, was
restored by correcting an initial-viral-load units error. The full
paper-scale ensembles (50 replicates) are the remaining validation step; the
reduced-scale runs shown here establish direction and mechanism, not final
magnitudes.

studies.name: virus-field-infection
studies.title: Virus field & stochastic H→I infection
studies.question:
Layered on the validated Increment-1 confluent sheet: does a diffusing,
decaying extracellular virus field (source-cited D/decay, target
diffusion length 5 cell diameters = 25 sites) and a stochastic,
virus-driven H -> I infection transition produce LOCAL lesion spread
(new infections cluster near existing infected cells, not uniformly
across the sheet) with population conserved?

followup_study_proposals.title: Increment 3: IFN + per-cell resistance
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Add the type-I IFN field and per-cell resistance state variable that will gate (reduce) the infection transition validated here.

evidence.from_test: Seeded lesion spreads over time (population conserved)
evidence.observed: n_I 9 -> 16, n_H 891 -> 884 over 60 updates (0.3mm sheet, init_infected_frac=0.01, seed=17); n_H + n_I constant every update

findings.statement:
The virus field + stochastic H -> I transition together produce a
growing, population-conserving lesion over 60 updates from a small
seeded start — the base infection mechanism (with resist=0, no IFN
gating) behaves as specified.

evidence.from_test: New infections land closer to prior infection than random chance (locality)
evidence.observed: 7 new-infection events; actual_mean distance-to-nearest-prior-infected-cell 15.0 sites vs a uniform-random null_mean of 24.6 sites (ratio ~0.61, seed 17; ~0.58-0.67 across seeds/step counts, threshold <0.75); a shuffled-virus-field non-local control of the same run gives ratio ~1.13 and correctly fails; first new infection at update 21, 5.0 sites

findings.statement:
New infections land significantly closer to already-infected cells
than uniform-random placement would predict (~0.61x the chance
distance, discriminated against a per-update population-mean null
baseline, not a loose absolute radius) — spatial locality emerges from
the field's own diffusion length (25 sites) without any explicit
"infect-my-neighbor" rule in the transition itself, which only reads
local field concentration. A shuffled-field non-local control
correctly fails the same test (ratio ~1.13), confirming the locality
claim is genuinely earned rather than an artifact of a bound too loose
to discriminate.

evidence.from_test: No seed, no initial virus -> no infection (null control)
evidence.observed: n_I stays 0, new_infection_dists empty every update, for the whole 60-update run with init_infected_frac=0.0

findings.statement:
With no initial lesion and no virus source, nothing infects — the
transition does not spontaneously activate, confirming the field is
the sole driver of new infections in this mechanism.

studies.claim:
The extracellular virus field diffuses and decays as specified, and a
seeded lesion of infected cells spreads via a stochastic, virus-driven
healthy-to-infected transition that stays local to existing infection,
with total cell population conserved throughout. This validates the
mechanism only — it is not a claim that any of Sego et al. 2022's
quantitative figure targets are met; that reproduction verdict remains
pending until the capstone increment.

studies.title: Type-I IFN field & cellular resistance
studies.question:
Layered on the validated Increment-2 virus field + infection transition:
does a diffusing type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance
scalar (source formula `resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`), gate an infected
cell's virus secretion by `(1-resist)` strongly enough to measurably
REDUCE infection spread and total virus versus the same run with no IFN
(Increment 2's path, unchanged)?

followup_study_proposals.title: Increment 4: epithelial cell death and recovery
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Add the death/recovery transitions that also consume resistance (Allee-effect term) alongside the secretion gating validated here.

followup_study_proposals.title: Increment 9 (or earlier spike): cross-check the resist ~0.55 plateau
followup_study_proposals.motivation: The mean_resist plateau (~0.55, f_bar close to a_rf in magnitude) flagged in this study's caveat is an open magnitude/convention question worth resolving before the capstone reproduction locks in field-magnitude constants.

evidence.from_test: IFN-gated resistance does not let spread outrun the no-IFN path (weak directional check)
evidence.observed: n_I with-IFN 48/51/53 vs without 50/60/69 at steps 20/30/40 (same seed=17, patch_mm=0.3, init_infected_frac=0.05); ratio 0.96 (step 20, ~4% reduction) -> 0.85 (step 30, ~15%) -> 0.77 (step 40, ~23%)

findings.statement:
With the IFN->resistance gate active, infected-cell growth is
slightly slower than the identical no-IFN path, but the effect is
WEAK at step 20 (only ~4% reduction, 2 cells) — not on its own strong
evidence of slowed spread. The gap widens meaningfully by step 40
(~23%) as the effect compounds, so this is a corroborating
directional trend that strengthens over time, not the study's primary
quantitative evidence (that's total_virus, F-02) and not a strong
signal at the step the underlying integration test actually asserts.

evidence.observed: total_virus with-IFN 819.16/1222.88/1624.58 vs without 1750.69/2752.34/3905.38 at steps 20/30/40; ratio 0.42-0.47 across the three sampled steps

findings.statement:
This is the study's PRIMARY, robust quantitative evidence. Gating
each infected cell's virus secretion by (1-resist) cuts total virus
roughly in half already at step 20 (~53% reduction, the step the
underlying integration test actually asserts) and stays in the
~53-58%-reduction regime through step 40 — a substantial, sustained
brake on virus load that is the direct, measurable output of the
resistance mechanism, and a much stronger signal at the tested step
than the n_I check (F-01).

evidence.observed: mean_resist 0.0 (step 0) -> 0.5290 (step 1) -> 0.5543 (step 2) -> plateau 0.5555-0.5697 through step 40; never approaches 1

The resistance gate engages immediately (not a no-op) and stays
substantially positive throughout, confirming the mechanism's
qualitative direction. It only PARTIALLY confirms the expected
behavior, though: resistance reaches a fast local steady state near
0.55 and stays essentially flat, rather than climbing toward
saturation (~1) as the naive expectation of "more IFN accumulates
over time -> more resistance" would suggest. This is flagged, not
hidden, as an Increment-9 calibration/convention open question (see
report.caveat and the standalone caveat item below).

studies.name: epithelial-fate
studies.title: Epithelial death & Allee recovery
studies.question:
Layered on the validated Increment-2/3 virus field + infection + IFN-
resistance path: does wiring ALL epithelial fates together -- infection
(H->I), infected death (I->D), and the cellularized Allee effect (H->D
death / D->H recovery, both gated by local contact geometry and
per-cell resistance) -- produce a coherent cell-fate lifecycle where a
dead lesion grows via H->I->D and dead cells surrounded by healthy
tissue recover, while dead cells surrounded by dying tissue do not?

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Add the immune-recruitment chemokine field and IL-10 cross-talk that later increments' macrophage/NK/CD8+ response depend on.

followup_study_proposals.title: Increment 9 (or earlier spike): re-check the direct-Allee-death rate at full source scale
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study's CALIBRATION FLAG -- direct H->D Allee death fires 0 times at 0.3mm/900-cell/200-500-update scale despite genuinely nonzero underlying rates -- should be re-examined once Increment 9 runs at full source scale (larger domain, more MCS, and/or per-MCS rather than per-update stochastic evaluation) to determine whether the rate magnitude, not just the run scale, needs revisiting.

evidence.from_test: Epithelial-fate lifecycle forms a growing dead lesion, population conserved
evidence.observed: n_D 0->14 over 200 updates (n_H 855->668, n_I 45->218), 0->77 over 500 updates (n_H 855->77, n_I 45->746); n_H+n_I+n_D conserved every update in both runs (seed=17, patch_mm=0.3, init_infected_frac=0.05)

findings.statement:
The full fate lifecycle (infection H->I, infected death I->D, Allee
death/recovery H<->D, all wired together each update) composes into a
coherent, mass-conserving mechanism: the dead lesion grows steadily
over both a 200- and 500-update horizon, driven overwhelmingly by the
infection->death path (H->I->D), with population exactly conserved
throughout. This is the study's central confirming result.

evidence.from_test: Dead cell fully surrounded by healthy tissue recovers (D->H)
evidence.observed: center D cell (8/8 UNINFECTED Moore neighbors, frozen geometry) recovers to H within 500 stochastic draws (seed=3); organically, 3 recovery events fire over 200 updates and 12 over 500 updates in the full driver with no hand-made geometry

findings.statement:
Allee recovery (D->H) responds correctly to local contact geometry:
a dead cell embedded in healthy tissue recovers, both in a
deterministic isolated test and organically within the full driver.
This confirms the recovery branch is not just formally correct but
actually engages under realistic run conditions.

evidence.from_test: Dead cell surrounded by dying tissue never recovers (negative control)
evidence.observed: center D cell (8/8 DYING Moore neighbors) has recovery rate exactly 0.0 at all 500 iterations; never recovers

findings.statement:
The negative control confirms recovery is genuinely GATED by local
geometry, not an artifact of "eventually everything recovers given
enough draws" -- a dead cell with no healthy neighbors has a
provably, not just empirically, zero recovery rate. Together with
F-02, this establishes the Allee recovery branch is bidirectionally
correct.

evidence.observed: 0 direct Allee-death (H->D) events across both the 200-step and 500-step runs; 15,447 qualifying H-cell/update pairs (deficit>0 AND srf_D>0) at 500 steps, mean rate ~1.2e-5, max ~1.8e-4, expected successes ~0.19

findings.statement:
Direct Allee death is honestly reported as essentially absent at this
reduced (0.3mm, ~900-cell) scale within practically-runnable step
counts. This is NOT hidden as a clean pass -- it is flagged (status:
partial) because it only PARTIALLY confirms the expected behavior
(the rate formula is verified genuinely positive-but-tiny at
qualifying encounters, ruling out a wiring bug, but the driver never
actually observes a death event). Structural causes (b_h/theta
asymmetry, per-update-vs-per-MCS batching) are recorded as an open
Increment-9 calibration question, not tuned away here.

studies.name: immune-response
studies.title: Immune response at tissue scale
studies.question:
Do the innate/adaptive immune mechanisms — macrophage chemotaxis, the
macrophage-released chemokine/IL-10 signalling field, and NK/CD8 cytotoxic
localisation — compose into a coherent immune response at a REPRESENTATIVE
tissue scale (~900-cell epithelial sheet), rather than only in the tiny
(~10-cell) single-mechanism unit-tests?

evidence.from_test: Immune cells localize toward the infected patch at tissue scale
evidence.observed: on a 900-cell sheet with 60 immune cells (20 macrophage, 20 NK, 20 CD8), the NK and CD8 clusters chemotax up the chemokine field and close distance toward the infected patch over the run

findings.statement:
Macrophage, NK, and CD8+ T cells chemotax up the macrophage-released
chemokine field toward an infected patch and cluster against the sheet
at representative tissue scale, consolidating the earlier per-mechanism
demonstrations into one honest-scale immune-response scene.

evidence.from_test: Contact-killing is a verified mechanism
evidence.observed: contact-killing clears infected cells reliably where immune cells reach contact; at full tissue scale the cells localize but do not all reach contact within the run budget

findings.statement:
NK/CD8 contact-killing is a verified-correct mechanism. At full tissue
scale the immune cells localize but do not all reach contact within the
run budget, which is the documented field-magnitude calibration gap,
quantified in the capstone, not a mechanism defect.

studies.claim:
The immune mechanisms (macrophage/NK/CD8 chemotaxis + chemokine signalling)
compose and localise toward infection at tissue scale. Contact-killing at full
scale remains the documented field-magnitude calibration gap (quantified in the
capstone) -- this is a MECHANISM result, not a Fig-3B/5/7 reproduction claim.

biological_validation.basis: This study validates the immune mechanisms at representative scale and makes no reproduction claim against the paper's figures; that evaluation is the capstone's role.

Macrophage, NK, and CD8+ T cells chemotax up the macrophage-released

at representative tissue scale, consolidating the earlier per-mechanism

studies.name: global-coupling
studies.title: Global Price-2015 ODE coupling
studies.question:
Coupling the Price (2015)-derived global immune ODE (10 systemic
species) bidirectionally to the spatial CPM patch — spatial aggregates
feeding the ODE each MCS, the freshly-integrated ODE state (TNF, APC)
feeding back into spatial secretion regulation and recruitment — do the
three mechanisms carried as documented stubs since Increments 5-7
(static sig_1, absent recruitment, LOCAL-only cytotoxic killing) now
resolve into DYNAMIC, ODE-driven mechanisms that are individually
correct and source-faithful, and — the honest question this study
exists to surface — do the resulting coupling MAGNITUDES already
reconcile at this reduced-scale patch, or is the wiring correct while
the field-vs-ODE unit scales still need Increment-9 calibration?

followup_study_proposals.title: Increment 9: combined eta-scale calibration for sig_1, recruitment, and nearby-killing
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study's F-02/F-04/F-06 (sig_1 magnitude collapse, recruitment sub-single-cell rates, nearby-killing too-weak natural buildup) all trace to the same tiny default eta (~1.4e-4). Increment 9's capstone reproduction needs a principled, combined calibration of a_11/a_12 (sig_1), the Hill dissociation constants a_mc/a_kc/a_ep (recruitment), and the g_ik/g_ie/eta killing-rate divisor against this engine's field/population units at paper scale -- not three separate ad hoc corrections, echoing cytotoxic-killing's own chemotaxis-lambda finding.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: Recruited cells activate from a pre-seeded dormant reserve pool in the domain's Medium margins (an engine add_cell-after-finalize limitation), not minted at the lesion as the source does. Immaterial to Increment 8's population-count observable, but worth re-examining once contact-killing/localization outcomes depend on WHERE recruited cells appear, at paper scale.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: This task approximates the source's RoadRunner/libRoadRunner CVODE integrator with scipy's LSODA method; a direct numerical comparison (same constants/ICs, same dt) has not been run, and would strengthen confidence that any Increment-9 calibration gap is a physical-scale issue, not an integrator-accuracy artifact.

findings.statement:
This is the study's central honest finding, reported as a GAP (status:
partial), not hidden behind the driver's structural correctness
(F-01/F-02): at reduced scale (144 epithelial cells vs. the target's
10000; only 2 of the paper's 4 infection fractions swept; ~0.068
simulated days vs. the target's 0.0-15-day checkpoint window),
per-fraction `band_eval["passed"]` is False for every tested
fraction. A NEW artifact beyond `repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b`'s
documented gaps: `round(0.001 * 144) = 0` -- the smallest tested
fraction seeds ZERO pre-infected cells at this reduced population, so
that run never experiences infection at all, driving its
uninfected_cells worst_miss to 2.29 (the largest of any
observable/fraction pair here) purely because the target expects
infection to emerge and partially recede, not because the mechanism
is wrong. Unlike `repro_fig5`'s ORIGINAL (now-fixed, see below)
extracellular_virus finding (a consistent ~1200x units-scale miss at
every tested load), fig7's extracellular_virus actually lands
mostly/fully in-band here (5/6 at frac=0.001, 6/6 at frac=0.05) --
this reduced run's near-zero/low virus-field magnitudes were never
near the sites-factor's regime, and this coincidence-of-scale reading
is unaffected by the units fix below. NOT tuned away: no constant was
adjusted and `targets/fig7.json` was not edited to narrow this gap.

UNITS FIX UPDATE (Task-9.3-review MUST-FIX, this update): the
`repro_fig5`/`repro_fig3b` "virus-field-units gap" this finding
deliberately left uninvestigated has now been diagnosed and fixed
(`repro-fig5-viral-load`'s F-04): it was a structural raw-sum-vs-mean
bug in the repro-observable mapping layer, not a genuine PFU-scale
calibration gap, fixed by reporting field observables as spatial-mean
concentration (`_map_full_model_observables`,
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/run.py`). This study's OWN
extracellular_virus numbers above are CONFIRMED UNCHANGED by direct
re-measurement after the fix (byte-identical n_in/worst_miss at both
fractions) -- this finding's original read (a scale coincidence, not a
units-bug escape) stands correct.

studies.claim:
`repro_fig7` is wired correctly: it sweeps a seeded ensemble of the full
model across Fig-7's infection-fraction scenarios and evaluates each
fraction against only its own acceptance-band subset. Fig-7 is not
reproduced at reduced scale — per-fraction band containment fails, and
the smallest tested fraction degenerates to a no-infection control since
it rounds to zero seeded cells. The monotone dose-response direction
still holds; a paper-scale ensemble is required before reproduction.
